method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, to the design decided for Michael (D1-D7 in NOTES.md) and the defaults ruled on 2026-10-18: a seat-neutral core (gva-core.l4, ten regulative rules) and one seat layer for three seats (gva-seat.l4), the seat a parameter that every exported question takes first; each regulative rule projected into does it apply, by when, have I complied (the rule run over the events inside the question with CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED) and what follows; no exported question takes a DEONTIC or EVENT input; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Compilation of the Graffiti Vandalism Act 2016 (No. 16 of 2016; Pt 1 from 11 Jul 2016, the rest from 12 Oct 2016), including the Local Government Legislation Amendment Act 2016 (No. 26 of 2016) Pt 3 Div 14 (from 21 Jan 2017); law_a147110, mrdoc 29645, retrieved 2026-09-07 from legislation.wa.gov.au, deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_29645.txt. Read, cited and not encoded: Sentencing Act 1995 s 9, Interpretation Act 1984 ss 61, 64, 71, State Administrative Tribunal Act 2004 s 92 and The Criminal Code s 731, all deposited under subjects/au/wa/.

checks.command: l4 run gva-dates.l4 ; l4 run gva-core.l4 ; l4 run gva-seat.l4 ; l4 run gva-cases-core.l4 ; l4 run gva-cases-seat.l4 ; l4 check gva-seat.l4
checks.result: 356 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in all five files (132 core + 224 seat, 2026-10-25); 22 #TRACEs in gva-cases-core.l4 with an expect line, each read and as expected (12 breaches, 6 rules still waiting, 2 permissions lapsed without a breach, 2 fulfilled after the lapse); l4 check gva-seat.l4: Check succeeded; a scan of the 38 @export blocks: each takes `my role` IS A Role first, none takes a DEONTIC or EVENT input
checks.consider_evaltrace: On 1.6.98 CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED works and OTHERWISE accepts a breached trace, but WHEN BREACH is a parse error and OTHERWISE cannot tell a breach from a pending rule; the seat helper therefore runs the rule over the act done, or over the act done now when it has not been, and so tells done in time, not done in time and still open apart correctly (NOTES.md finding 20)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: In: ss 3, 4 (adult, child, graffiti implement, offender, possession), 5, 6, 7 (with the s 7(2) defence), 8, 10, 12, 13, 14 (public place, as a gloss), 18(1)-(5), 19(3)-(7), 20, 21, 22(1)-(2), 23, 24(1), (3), 25, 27, 28, 29 (the warrant as an input), 30. Out: ss 1, 2, 9, 11, 15-17, 22(3), 26 (noted), 31, 32, 33-44. Judgments are inputs answered conditionally. The Interpretation Act s 61(1)(e) move of a last day off a weekend or public holiday is not encoded.

regulative_rules: s 5(1) -- a person must not damage another person's property by graffiti without consent
s 6(1) -- a person must not possess a thing with the intention of applying graffiti with it
s 7 -- a person must not sell a graffiti implement to a child, unless they believed on reasonable grounds the buyer was an adult
s 18(2), (5) -- the notice recipient must ensure the graffiti is obliterated within the time in the notice
s 19(3), (4) -- the local government may obliterate the graffiti and recover its reasonable cost
s 22(2) -- the affected person may object within 28 days after the notice is given, or any further time allowed
s 23(3) -- the affected person may apply for review within 42 days after the right to apply arose
s 24(1) -- the notice is suspended until the objection or application is decided
s 25(1) -- the local government may obliterate graffiti applied without consent
ss 27, 28 -- the local government may enter only with consent, a warrant, or at least 24 hours' notice
